sections.start: This data has front and back pocket measurements for 80 pairs of jeans, 40 men's and 40 women's , from 20 popular brands.
sections.serves: Women's jeans come with shallower front pockets
sections.how: It introduces the dataset and states the main comparison that women's front pockets are much shallower than men's, with back pockets about the same.

sections.start: Men's front pockets run from 20.0 to 28.0 deep; women's run from 11.5 to 21.5.
sections.serves: Front pockets: two groups that barely overlap
sections.how: It gives the two ranges, shows only one women's pair reaches the shallowest men's pocket, and reports lower average depth and width for women's front pockets.

sections.start: Back pockets are close in size: men's average 16.0 high and 13.7 wide, women's 15.1 high and 13.3 wide.
sections.serves: The gap is in the front, not the back
sections.how: It shows back-pocket averages are close and that women's front pockets are often shallower than their back pockets, while men's never are, locating the gap in front.

sections.start: Each brand in the data sells two men's and two women's pairs.
sections.how: It reports that in all 20 brands men's front pockets are deeper on average, with the gap ranging from 2.5 to 13.4 cm.

sections.start: For women, cut makes little difference: average front pocket depth is 14.3 for skinny, 14.4 for straight and 14.2 for boot-cut jeans.
sections.serves: Neither cut nor price fixes it
sections.how: It shows cut changes average front-pocket depth little and price correlates negatively or near zero with depth, so neither raises women's pocket depth.
